intro: Hi! Today you learn how to invite people (Would you like to…? How about…?), how to say yes or no kindly, and how to agree on a time and a place to meet. Warm-up: how would you ask a colleague to go for coffee after work?
teachingNotes: Invitation forms: Would you like to + base verb? (polite, for anyone: boss, client, new people), Do you want to + base verb? (friendly, for friends), Let's + base verb (known from A1: no to, no 'we': *'Let's to go', *'Let's we go'), Shall we + base verb? (teach only as a phrase: 'yuk kita…?'; more common in British English, Americans often say 'Do you want to…?' or 'Should we…?'). Common errors: *'Would you like come?' (missing to), *'Shall we to go?', and 'Do you like…?' used as an invitation (it asks what someone enjoys in general).

The node's common error: *'How about go to the cinema?' → 'How about going to the cinema?'. Explain why: 'about' is a preposition (kata depan, like in, on, at), and after a preposition English needs a noun or a verb + -ing, the name of the activity, as in 'I like swimming'. Indonesian 'gimana kalau pergi' doesn't change the verb. How about = What about. They also take a noun: How about a coffee? How about Saturday? How about 7? Don't confuse with 'How about you?' (asking back, A1).

Accepting: 'Sure, I'd love to!' (I'd = I would; 'to' stands for the verb from the question, so *'Yes, I'd love.' is wrong; 'I'd like to' is also correct), 'That sounds great!' / 'Sounds good!' (sound = kedengarannya), 'Good idea!', 'Yes, let's!' (after Let's / Shall we). Never *'Yes, I like.' Declining in three parts: I'm sorry, I can't. + a short reason (present continuous for fixed arrangements: I'm working on Saturday; or I'm busy / I have a meeting) + an alternative (Maybe another time? / How about Sunday?). Watch *'I busy' (missing am) and *'No, I don't want' (too direct, sounds rude).

Culture, with respect: in Indonesia a soft, open answer ('insya Allah', 'lihat nanti ya', 'kayaknya bisa') is a kind habit that avoids a direct no. Never mock it; many Muslim English speakers say insya Allah too. Just explain that an English speaker usually hears 'Maybe' / 'We'll see' as a possible yes and may wait for the person, so a clear, friendly no + reason is the kind answer in English. If the learner really doesn't know yet: 'I'm not sure yet. I'll tell you tomorrow.'

Arranging: When shall we meet? / Where shall we meet? / What time is good for you? / Are you free on Saturday? / Is Saturday OK for you? / How about 7? / Let's meet at 7 at the station. / See you on Saturday! / I'll see you there. Prepositions from A1: at + clock time and at + a meeting point (at the station, at Sari's house), on + a day (on Saturday, on Friday evening), nothing before tomorrow, tonight, this…, next… (*'see you on tomorrow'). Time trap: 'setengah tujuh' = 6:30 = half past six; British 'half seven' = 7:30. Running late: 'Sorry, I'm going to be late. I'll be there at 7:15.'

Limits: the chain is going to, will, the present continuous and A1. No past simple (except was/were) and no present perfect (no 'I've already got plans', 'I saw that film'), no 'have to' (use 'I'm working'), no could/might, no conditionals ('If you're free…' → 'Are you free…?'). 'shall' only in Shall we…? and When/Where shall we meet?. 'Do you fancy…?' is British: explain it only if the learner asks. Contexts: kantor, warung, mall, KRL station, futsal, night market, weddings.

keyPoints.title: Inviting: Would you like to…? How about…?
keyPoints.explanation: Would you like to + verb? is polite for anyone; Do you want to + verb? is friendly, for friends; Let's + verb and Shall we + verb? suggest doing something together (no to after them). How about / What about + a noun or a verb + -ing: How about going…?, never 'How about go'.

examples.en: Would you like to have lunch with us?
How about going to the cinema?

id.title: Mengajak: Would you like to…? How about…?
id.explanation: Would you like to + kata kerja? sopan untuk siapa saja; Do you want to + kata kerja? lebih akrab, untuk teman; Let's + kata kerja dan Shall we + kata kerja? mengajak melakukan sesuatu bersama (tanpa to setelahnya). How about / What about + kata benda atau kata kerja + -ing: How about going…?, bukan 'How about go'.

keyPoints.title: Yes or no, kindly and clearly
keyPoints.explanation: Say yes warmly: Sure, I'd love to! / That sounds great! / Good idea! Keep the to in I'd love to. Say no in three parts: I'm sorry, I can't. + a short reason (I'm working on Saturday.) + another time (Maybe another time? / How about Sunday?). A vague 'Maybe' sounds like a possible yes to an English speaker.

examples.en: I'm sorry, I can't. I'm working on Saturday.
examples.id: Maaf, aku nggak bisa. Hari Sabtu aku kerja.

id.title: Ya atau tidak, dengan ramah dan jelas
id.explanation: Terima dengan hangat: Sure, I'd love to! / That sounds great! / Good idea! Jangan lupa to di I'd love to. Tolak dalam tiga bagian: I'm sorry, I can't. + alasan singkat (I'm working on Saturday.) + lain kali (Maybe another time? / How about Sunday?). Jawaban samar seperti 'Maybe' terdengar seperti 'mungkin bisa' bagi penutur bahasa Inggris.

keyPoints.title: Arranging a time and place
keyPoints.explanation: Ask: When shall we meet? / Where shall we meet? / Is Saturday OK for you? Suggest: How about 7? / Let's meet at 7 at the station. Finish: See you on Saturday! / I'll see you there. Use at + a clock time or a meeting point, on + a day, and no small word before tomorrow, tonight or next.

examples.en: Let's meet at 7 at the station.

id.title: Menentukan waktu dan tempat
id.explanation: Tanya: When shall we meet? / Where shall we meet? / Is Saturday OK for you? Usulkan: How about 7? / Let's meet at 7 at the station. Tutup: See you on Saturday! / I'll see you there. Pakai at + jam atau tempat bertemu, on + hari, dan tanpa kata depan sebelum tomorrow, tonight atau next.

assessment.rubric: Correct: on (a named day, even with evening). 'in' = 0 ('in Friday evening' is wrong: with a day, use on). 'at' = 0.

blocks.text:
An **invitation** (*ajakan* or *undangan*) asks someone to do something with you. Here are four ways:
- **Would you like to** + verb …? Polite, good for anyone: your boss, a client, a new friend. You know *would like* from A1: here it's a polite *mau*, not *akan*.
- **Do you want to** + verb …? Friendly and relaxed, for friends and family.
- **Let's** + verb. You know it already: *Let's go!* = *Ayo kita pergi!*
- **Shall we** + verb …? Learn it as a phrase that means *Yuk kita …?* Here *shall* just makes a friendly question about doing something together.

After **like** and **want** comes **to**. After **Let's** and **Shall we**, no *to*. In all four, the verb is the **base form** (the verb as in the dictionary: no -s, no -ing).

id.text:
**Ajakan** atau **undangan** (*invitation*) meminta seseorang melakukan sesuatu bersamamu. Ini empat caranya:
- **Would you like to** + kata kerja …? Sopan, cocok untuk siapa saja: atasan, klien, teman baru. Kamu sudah kenal *would like* dari A1: di sini artinya *mau* yang sopan, bukan *akan*.
- **Do you want to** + kata kerja …? Akrab dan santai, untuk teman dan keluarga.
- **Let's** + kata kerja. Kamu sudah tahu: *Let's go!* = *Ayo kita pergi!*
- **Shall we** + kata kerja …? Hafalkan sebagai ungkapan yang artinya *Yuk kita …?* Di sini *shall* hanya membuat pertanyaan ramah untuk melakukan sesuatu bersama.

Setelah **like** dan **want** ada **to**. Setelah **Let's** dan **Shall we**, tidak ada *to*. Di keempatnya, kata kerjanya **bentuk dasar** (seperti di kamus: tanpa -s, tanpa -ing).

rows.en: Would you like to have lunch with us?
Do you want to come to my house on Sunday?
rows.id: Mau main ke rumahku hari Minggu?

rows.note: no to, no we after Let's

id.note: tanpa to dan tanpa we setelah Let's

rows.en: Shall we go to the night market?
rows.note: more common in British English; Americans often say Do you want to…?

id.note: lebih umum di bahasa Inggris British; orang Amerika sering bilang Do you want to…?

blocks.text: **Would you like to or Do you want to?** Indonesian *mau* covers both. With friends, *Do you want to…?* is normal and friendly. With your boss, a client or someone older, *Would you like to…?* is safer. In fast speech *want to* often sounds like 'wanna': fine to understand, but write *want to*. And don't drop **to**: *Would you like to come?*, not 'Would you like come?'. Also, **Do you like…?** is not an invitation: it asks what someone enjoys in general (*suka*).

id.text: **Would you like to atau Do you want to?** Kata *mau* mencakup keduanya. Dengan teman, *Do you want to…?* biasa dan akrab. Dengan atasan, klien atau orang yang lebih tua, *Would you like to…?* lebih aman. Saat bicara cepat, *want to* sering terdengar seperti 'wanna': boleh dipahami, tapi tulislah *want to*. Dan jangan buang **to**: *Would you like to come?*, bukan 'Would you like come?'. Lalu, **Do you like…?** bukan ajakan: itu bertanya apa yang disukai seseorang secara umum (*suka*).

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan is new in your office. Invite him politely.
options: Would you like have lunch with us?
Would you like to have lunch with us?
Do you like having lunch with us?
blocks.explain: A polite invitation is Would you like **to** + verb. Without to it's wrong, and Do you like…? asks what he enjoys in general, it isn't an invitation.

id.prompt: Pak Hasan baru di kantormu. Ajak dia dengan sopan.
id.explain: Ajakan yang sopan adalah Would you like **to** + kata kerja. Tanpa to salah, dan Do you like…? bertanya apa yang dia sukai secara umum, bukan ajakan.

blocks.text:
**How about …?** and **What about …?** mean the same: *Gimana kalau …?* They make a suggestion. After them, put:
- a **noun** (*kata benda*: the name of a thing, a place or a time): *How about a coffee? How about Saturday? How about 7?*
- or a **verb + -ing**: *How about going to the cinema? What about cooking at home tonight?*

Why not 'How about go'? **about** is a small word like *in, on, at*: a **preposition** (*kata depan*). After a preposition, English needs a 'thing' word. So the verb takes **-ing** and becomes the name of the activity, just like *swimming* in *I like swimming*. Indonesian *gimana kalau pergi* doesn't change *pergi*, so learners say 'How about go'. Say **How about going**.

id.text:
**How about …?** dan **What about …?** artinya sama: *Gimana kalau …?* Keduanya dipakai untuk mengusulkan sesuatu. Setelahnya, taruh:
- **kata benda** (*noun*: nama benda, tempat atau waktu): *How about a coffee? How about Saturday? How about 7?*
- atau **kata kerja + -ing**: *How about going to the cinema? What about cooking at home tonight?*

Kenapa bukan 'How about go'? **about** adalah kata kecil seperti *in, on, at*: **kata depan** (*preposition*). Setelah kata depan, bahasa Inggris butuh kata 'benda'. Jadi kata kerjanya diberi **-ing** dan menjadi nama kegiatan, sama seperti *swimming* di *I like swimming*. Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *gimana kalau pergi* tidak mengubah kata *pergi*, makanya banyak yang bilang 'How about go'. Yang benar **How about going**.

rows.en: How about going to the cinema?
rows.note: about + verb-ing · cinema is British; Americans say the movies

id.note: about + kata kerja-ing · cinema itu British; orang Amerika bilang the movies

rows.en: What about cooking at home tonight?
rows.id: Gimana kalau nanti malam masak di rumah?

blocks.text: No **to** after about either: 'How about to go' is wrong. And don't mix it up with **How about you?** from A1: that asks the same question back (*kalau kamu?*). The word after *about* tells you which one it is: *you* → asking back; *going, a coffee, Saturday* → a suggestion.

id.text: Setelah about juga tidak ada **to**: 'How about to go' salah. Jangan tertukar dengan **How about you?** dari A1: itu menanyakan balik (*kalau kamu?*). Kata setelah *about* menunjukkan yang mana: *you* → bertanya balik; *going, a coffee, Saturday* → usulan.

blocks.prompt: Complete: It's Sari's birthday tomorrow. How about ___ her a cake?
blocks.explain: After about (a preposition), use a noun or a verb + -ing: How about **buying** her a cake? 'buy' is a word-by-word translation of *beli*, and there's no to after about.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Besok ulang tahun Sari. How about ___ her a cake?
id.explain: Setelah about (kata depan), pakai kata benda atau kata kerja + -ing: How about **buying** her a cake? 'buy' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *beli*, dan tidak ada to setelah about.

blocks.text:
**Yes:** say it warmly.
- **Sure, I'd love to!** (*Mau banget!*) **I'd** = I would. Why does it end with **to**? English doesn't repeat the verb from the question: *Would you like to come? — I'd love to (come).* So keep **to**: 'Yes, I'd love' is wrong, and 'Yes, I like' is wrong too.
- **That sounds great!** or **Sounds good!** (*Kedengarannya asyik!*): *sound* = *kedengarannya*, with -s because *that* is like *it*.
- **Good idea!** or **Yes, let's!** after *Let's…* or *Shall we…?*

**No:** say it kindly **and** clearly, in three small parts:
1. **I'm sorry, I can't.** (or *Thanks for asking, but I can't.*)
2. a short **reason**. For a plan fixed with someone, use the present continuous you know (am / is / are + verb-ing): *I'm working on Saturday. I'm visiting my grandma.*
3. **another time**: *Maybe another time?* or *How about Sunday?*

id.text:
**Ya:** ucapkan dengan hangat.
- **Sure, I'd love to!** (*Mau banget!*) **I'd** = I would. Kenapa diakhiri **to**? Bahasa Inggris tidak mengulang kata kerja dari pertanyaannya: *Would you like to come? — I'd love to (come).* Jadi **to** tetap ada: 'Yes, I'd love' salah, dan 'Yes, I like' juga salah.
- **That sounds great!** atau **Sounds good!** (*Kedengarannya asyik!*): *sound* = *kedengarannya*, pakai -s karena *that* sama seperti *it*.
- **Good idea!** atau **Yes, let's!** setelah *Let's…* atau *Shall we…?*

**Tidak:** ucapkan dengan ramah **dan** jelas, dalam tiga bagian kecil:
1. **I'm sorry, I can't.** (atau *Thanks for asking, but I can't.*)
2. **alasan** singkat. Untuk rencana yang sudah pasti dengan orang lain, pakai present continuous yang sudah kamu kenal (am / is / are + kata kerja-ing): *I'm working on Saturday. I'm visiting my grandma.*
3. **lain kali**: *Maybe another time?* atau *How about Sunday?*

rows.en: Would you like to come to my party? — Sure, I'd love to!
rows.id: Mau datang ke pestaku? — Mau banget!

rows.en: Let's have bakso after work! — Good idea!
rows.id: Yuk makan bakso pulang kerja! — Ide bagus!

rows.en: Do you want to go to Bogor on Sunday? — Sorry, I can't. I'm visiting my parents. Maybe another time?
rows.id: Mau ke Bogor hari Minggu? — Maaf, aku nggak bisa. Aku mau ke rumah orang tuaku. Lain kali, ya?

rows.en: Thanks for asking, but I'm busy tonight. How about tomorrow?
rows.id: Makasih udah ngajak, tapi malam ini aku sibuk. Gimana kalau besok?

blocks.text: **Insya Allah, lihat nanti ya, kayaknya bisa…** In Indonesia, a soft, open answer is a kind habit: it avoids a direct *no*. *Insya Allah* is a beautiful phrase, and many Muslim English speakers use it too. But when an English speaker hears *Maybe* or *We'll see*, they usually think you might come, and they may wait for you or keep a seat for you. So if you know you can't come, the kind answer in English is a clear, friendly **no + reason**: *I'm sorry, I can't. I'm working late.* If you really don't know yet, say that, and say when you'll answer: *I'm not sure yet. I'll tell you tomorrow.*

id.text: **Insya Allah, lihat nanti ya, kayaknya bisa…** Di Indonesia, jawaban yang lembut dan terbuka adalah kebiasaan yang sopan: tidak langsung bilang *tidak*. *Insya Allah* adalah ungkapan yang indah, dan banyak penutur bahasa Inggris yang Muslim juga memakainya. Tapi saat penutur bahasa Inggris mendengar *Maybe* atau *We'll see*, biasanya mereka mengira kamu mungkin datang, lalu menunggumu atau menyiapkan tempat untukmu. Jadi kalau kamu tahu tidak bisa datang, jawaban yang sopan dalam bahasa Inggris adalah **tidak + alasan** yang jelas dan ramah: *I'm sorry, I can't. I'm working late.* Kalau kamu memang belum tahu, katakan itu, dan sebutkan kapan kamu akan memberi jawaban: *I'm not sure yet. I'll tell you tomorrow.*

blocks.text: Avoid **No, I don't want.** It sounds rude in English, like *Nggak mau!* And remember **am** in your reason: *I'm busy*, not 'I busy' (Indonesian *aku sibuk* has no *am*).

id.text: Hindari **No, I don't want.** Dalam bahasa Inggris itu terdengar kasar, seperti *Nggak mau!* Dan ingat **am** di alasanmu: *I'm busy*, bukan 'I busy' (*aku sibuk* tidak punya kata *am*).

options: Sorry, I can't. I busy on Saturday.
Sorry, I can't. I'm busy on Saturday.
Sorry, I not can. I'm busy on Saturday.
blocks.explain: **I'm busy** needs am (I'm = I am), even though *aku sibuk* has no extra word. The negative of can is **can't** (cannot), not 'not can'.

id.prompt: Jawaban mana yang benar dalam bahasa Inggris?
id.explain: **I'm busy** butuh am (I'm = I am), walaupun *aku sibuk* tidak punya kata tambahan. Bentuk negatif can adalah **can't** (cannot), bukan 'not can'.

blocks.text:
After *yes*, agree on the **time** and the **place**.
- Ask: **When shall we meet?** **Where shall we meet?** **What time is good for you?** **Are you free on Saturday?** **Is Saturday OK for you?**
- Suggest: **How about 7?** **Let's meet at 7 at the station.**
- Finish: **Great, see you on Saturday!** **OK, I'll see you there.** (I'll = I will: a promise.)

The small words from A1:
- **at** + a clock time: *at 7, at half past six*
- **on** + a day: *on Saturday, on Saturday morning*
- **at** + a meeting point: *at the station, at the café, at Sari's house*
- **no word** before *tomorrow, tonight, this…, next…*: *See you tomorrow*, not 'See you on tomorrow'.

id.text:
Setelah *ya*, sepakati **waktu** dan **tempat**nya.
- Tanya: **When shall we meet?** **Where shall we meet?** **What time is good for you?** **Are you free on Saturday?** **Is Saturday OK for you?**
- Usulkan: **How about 7?** **Let's meet at 7 at the station.**
- Tutup: **Great, see you on Saturday!** **OK, I'll see you there.** (I'll = I will: janji.)

Kata depan dari A1:
- **at** + jam: *at 7, at half past six*
- **on** + hari: *on Saturday, on Saturday morning*
- **at** + tempat bertemu: *at the station, at the café, at Sari's house*
- **tanpa kata depan** sebelum *tomorrow, tonight, this…, next…*: *See you tomorrow*, bukan 'See you on tomorrow'.

rows.en: Let's meet at 7 at the station.
Sorry, I'm going to be late. I'll be there at 7:15.
rows.id: Maaf, aku bakal telat. Aku sampai jam 7.15.

blocks.text: **Time trap:** *setengah tujuh* is **6:30** = *half past six*, not seven! And in British English people also say **half seven** for **7:30**. When you're not sure, check: *Half seven? You mean 7:30?* Writing the numbers (*6:30*) in a message avoids mistakes.

id.text: **Jebakan jam:** *setengah tujuh* itu **6:30** = *half past six*, bukan jam tujuh! Dan di bahasa Inggris British, orang juga bilang **half seven** untuk **7:30**. Kalau ragu, pastikan: *Half seven? You mean 7:30?* Menulis angkanya (*6:30*) di pesan membantu menghindari salah paham.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Let's meet ___ the café ___ Saturday.
blocks.explain: **at** + a meeting point (at the café) and **on** + a day (on Saturday).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Let's meet ___ the café ___ Saturday.
id.explain: **at** + tempat bertemu (at the café) dan **on** + hari (on Saturday).

id.intro: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar cara mengajak orang (Would you like to…? How about…?), cara bilang ya atau tidak dengan ramah, dan cara menyepakati waktu serta tempat bertemu. Pemanasan: bagaimana kamu mengajak rekan kerja ngopi sepulang kerja?
suggestedQuestions: Apakah 'Do you want to…?' tidak sopan?
Apa yang bisa kuucapkan selain 'insya Allah' kalau aku belum yakin bisa datang?
Kenapa 'How about going', bukan 'How about go'?
Apa bedanya Let's dan Shall we?

assessment.mp-1: Lengkapi ajakan ini dengan kata kerja watch: Would you like ___ a film with me on Saturday?
assessment.mp-2: Temukan kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: How about eat at the warung tonight?
assessment.mp-3: Dengarkan ajakan Sari. Kamu mau datang. Terima dengan hangat. Lengkapi: Yes, I'd ___ ___!
assessment.mp-4: Bu Ani mengajakmu makan malam hari Jumat, tapi hari itu atasanmu memintamu tetap di kantor sampai jam 9 malam. Lengkapi jawaban sopanmu dengan present continuous dari work: I'm sorry, I can't. I ___ late on Friday.
assessment.mp-5: Kamu tidak bisa datang ke pertandingan futsal Budi malam ini, tapi kamu ingin datang lain kali. Setelah 'Sorry, I can't.', tambahkan pertanyaan yang ramah. Lengkapi: Maybe ___ ___?
assessment.mp-6: Temanmu bertanya: 'Where shall we meet?' Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris dengan Let's meet dan tempat ini: Gambir Station.
assessment.mp-7: Lengkapi dengan satu kata: See you ___ Friday evening!
